head: 0af8d058b21d8ecb7846f8265bb06211a0f68a12
summary:
This attempt closes O-079, O-080 and O-081. All three changes are in the person-run pool judge (`tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1`) and its tests; `src` is untouched.
- **O-079 (settle gate):** the gate is now as strict as the drift VOID it protects. Each gap must move both pools slower than 3 × spike 3's 10,936 B/s, about 1.88 MiB a minute, instead of under 16 MiB a gap.
- **O-080 (cancel and close runs):** `Invoke-ExeArm` now records `acted`. A cancel or close run whose hook never acted, or a cancel whose report is not Cancelled, gives UNDECIDED and names the hook's refused line.
- **O-081 (guard stops on S/P):** an S or P arm the guard stopped is now over T with no projection. S stopped alone gives B; P stopped gives C.

Running the protocol under Windows PowerShell 5.1 also exposed a harness defect: every `hookLog` line was serialised as a ~200 KB object, about 2 MB per arm line, and the refused line could not be read back. It is fixed.

Results:
- PoolWatchReportTests: 41/41 pass. 10 of the new rows fail against the previous script, so they would have caught these bugs.
- The 5.1 smoke protocol ran end to end.
- Every new judge branch gives the intended outcome under 5.1 on patched real smoke logs.
- Full suite: 573 passed; the 3 failures are the known last-access tests.
- The repro exits 0.

files.why: O-079: the settle gate is now a rate tied to the drift VOID (DriftDisagree × IdleDriftSeen = 32,808 B/s), applied per gap of at least MarkEverySec, and the VOID reason and the -Protocol warning say so. O-080: Invoke-ExeArm records `acted`. The ten-run check gives UNDECIDED when a cancel or close run never acted (naming the hook's refused line) or when a cancel's report is not Cancelled; old logs fall back to the hookLog lines. O-081: a guard-stopped S or P skips the summary and projection and counts as over T; S stopped alone gives B, and P stopped (with S stopped or over T) gives C. Read-Lines replaces Get-Content wherever lines are written back as JSON (hook logs, trigger checks, the fltmc paste), because 5.1's ConvertTo-Json serialised each line as a ~200 KB provider object.

New rows:
- O-079: settle-gate-on-10-mib-gaps (VOID for the settle, not the drift) and boot-settles-slowly (A).
- O-080: close-app-shut-down-before-trigger, cancel-trigger-deadline and cancel-not-cancelled (each UNDECIDED).
- O-081: probe-guard-stop now gives S a null summary and exit -1, as a killed ScanArm leaves it; probe-and-plain-guard-stop and probe-over-plain-guard-stop give C.

Three new Facts pin the exact reasons. The run builder writes `acted` and `hookLog` lines and Cancelled reports for the stop arms, and its settle phases are now data-driven.

obligations.how: I made the settle gate as strict as the VOID rule it protects. `$Tolerance.SettleRateBytesPerSec = DriftDisagree × IdleDriftSeen = 3 × 10,936 = 32,808 B/s`, which is 1.88 MiB per 60 s gap. That is derived, not rounded up to 2 MiB, because 2 MiB sits above the VOID threshold. Test-Settled, which both -Protocol's Wait-Settle and -Report use, requires each of the last two gaps to move both pools by less than that rate × max(gap, MarkEverySec). The 30-minute cap and the early stop are kept. The VOID reason now gives the gap, its length and the limit. Rows: settle-gate-on-10-mib-gaps (two 10 MiB gaps, the old gate's pass, then I0 growing 2 MiB a minute) gives VOID 'the boot had not settled ... paged 10.0 MiB ... in 60 s, against 1.88 MiB a minute', never the drift reason; boot-settles-slowly (85, then 10, then 1 MiB gaps) gives A. Fact: TheSettleGateIsAsStrictAsTheDriftRuleItProtects. The tolerance row text is updated. The engine's own record of the R2-N1/O-076 discharge still says 16 MiB, and I cannot edit it: the current rule is 1.88 MiB a minute.

Invoke-ExeArm records `acted = [bool](@($acted) -match '^acted ')`. In Get-Verdict's ten-run check, any exe-cancel or exe-close arm that did not act and did not run to the end gives UNDECIDED, naming the arm and the hook's refused line, e.g. 'closed run X4 never stopped the scan: the hook logged 'refused mode=close reason=the app shut down before the trigger' (exit 70)'. An exe-cancel whose report.status is not 'Cancelled' gives UNDECIDED too. Guard-stopped arms still count as over T, and runs that ended before the trigger keep their existing message. Rows close-app-shut-down-before-trigger, cancel-trigger-deadline and cancel-not-cancelled are in TheReportRoutesARunAsTheToleranceRowSays, with the exact reasons pinned in CancelledOrClosedRunsCountOnlyWhenTheHookActed. Checked under 5.1 on patched real smoke logs: all three, plus an old log with no acted field, give UNDECIDED with the hook line.

In the S/P projection loop, an arm with guardStop set is skipped before the summary check, so a killed ScanArm's null summary no longer reads 'file count is missing'. That arm counts as over T. Routing:
- S stopped while P is within T: B.
- Both over T with a stop involved: the excess rule, reading 'stopped' as a projection past anything measured. S stopped and P not gives B; P stopped, with S stopped or only over T, gives C.

The probe-guard-stop row now feeds S a null summary and exit -1. Rows probe-and-plain-guard-stop and probe-over-plain-guard-stop (C) are added. AGuardStoppedProbeOrPlainOpenWithNoSummaryIsOverT pins all three reasons. Under 5.1 on patched smoke logs: S stopped gives B, both stopped gives C.

deviations: O-079: the gate is a rate over each gap, measured over at least MarkEverySec, not a fixed '2 MiB per gap'. The two are identical for the protocol's real 60 s gaps. I first built a pure rate, and the 5.1 smoke protocol could not settle: its 2 s gaps turn ordinary pool churn of a few hundred KB into rates far above the limit. Measured: 31 settle marks in 60 s and never settled, so the run stopped before I0. With the max(gap, MarkEverySec) floor, smoke settled at settle/02-03. The limit is derived as 1.88 MiB a minute rather than rounded up to 2 MiB, because 2 MiB would sit above the 3× drift VOID it protects.

Beyond the three obligations: the 5.1 smoke run showed that Invoke-ExeArm's hookLog, -Prepare's triggerChecks and Read-FltmcPaste write Get-Content lines into JSON. Windows PowerShell 5.1, the shell the person runs -Protocol in, serialises each line as an object carrying its PSPath, PSDrive and provider, making each arm line about 2.1 MB. The refused line O-080's message names could then not be read back. This is a defect in this slice's own harness, on the path O-080 depends on, so I fixed it with a Read-Lines helper ([IO.File]::ReadAllLines). After the fix, arms.jsonl was 6,450 bytes with plain-string hook lines.

Rows beyond the ones asked: cancel-not-cancelled (O-080's report-status clause had no row) and probe-over-plain-guard-stop (exercises the P-stopped branch). Neither changes behaviour beyond the obligations.
follow_ups: This is a loop. Build attempts 2, 3, 4 and now 5 were each sent back by code-review findings against the person-run judge tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1, with no src change. Each finding was real and cheap, but the judge's edges can always be extended one step further. DONE (c) cannot be decided until the person's Restart and -Prepare/-Protocol anyway. A person may want to rule that further judge refinements go to a follow-up slice rather than holding SL-095's merge.

If the guard stops arm L, -Protocol sizes S and P from `$l.summary`, and a killed ScanArm prints none. S and P then run over 1 file each, and -Report reads UNDECIDED for L's missing file count. ScanArm should write its listed count progressively, or -Protocol should count L.files.txt.

What remains of R3-1: the gate assumes I1 drifts like spike 3's 10,936 B/s. If the session's I1 is quieter, an I0 just under the gate's rate can still VOID on drift. The finding's alternative would close that: compare I0's first-half and second-half drift before L, and extend I0 rather than proceed.

Smoke cannot show an acted Cancel. The 2,005-folder smoke tree is listed inside one 250 ms tick, so every -Prepare and -Protocol trigger logged 'the scan ended before the trigger'. Only WindowCases X-003's 30,150-folder tree proves the triggers act. A -Smoke option that uses such a tree would let smoke exercise acted=True end to end.

Residue: my check of the new tests against the HEAD script left a copy of PoolWatch.ps1 at C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\pw-new-<guid>.ps1, because this shell's TEMP resolves there and deleting it was denied. It is about 60 KB and harmless, but I cannot remove it.

On this machine, Windows PowerShell 5.1's Add-Type fails when TEMP is C:\WINDOWS\TEMP ('Source file ... could not be found'), so -Protocol under 5.1 needs a writable TEMP. The person's own session has a per-user TEMP, so this should not affect the real run, but -Prepare could check it.

not_built: DONE (c) itself is not decided. It needs the person's -Prepare, a Start > Restart, and -Protocol under docs/design/SL-095-runs/ (Q-184, Q-185). Nothing in this build can stand in for a fresh boot.

For O-079 I did not build the finding's alternative safeguard (compare I0's first-half and second-half drift before L, and extend I0). The finding offered it as an alternative to tightening the gate, and the gate was tightened. It is listed as a follow-up for the remaining I1-quieter-than-spike-3 case.

architecture.find: It records every folder it could not open instead of dropping it silently.
architecture.replace: It records every folder it could not open instead of dropping it silently. It never lists the Windows container layer store (%ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers) or anything in it, and it finds the store by path, not by attributes, once per scan before anything is listed. A scan above the store records it as one folder not scanned and never opened, its size not counted and kept apart from the unreadable folders. A root at or inside the store is refused with nothing listed or probed. Only a root that reaches the store under another spelling, such as a junction or subst drive, is opened once to find its final path. This holds while the precaution against wcifs.sys's leak (microsoft/Windows-Containers#646) is on, as it is unless the person turns it off.
architecture.why: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/ContainerLayerStore.cs:59 (internal static class ContainerLayerStore: Resolve, string check then handle check), Scanner's FolderDone exclusion and SkippedStores, and DirectoryReader.Read's backstop.
